title: GovernanceProjection — the governance skills' output contract
description: One envelope carrying every governance reconstruction output. Proposed under TDR-0034 and NOT accepted. This is a skill-output contract, not a record schema and not a fourth interchange structure: it sits downstream of SourceFragment, RecordContribution and CandidateAssembly and amends none of them (TDR-0022). A projection carries interpretation about organisational meaning, never organisational meaning itself, so it fails question 1 of the record admission test by design and can never be promoted to a record. Epistemic state is assessed per claim, never per document or per projection. Known projection types validate strictly against their own payload; an unknown type is permitted a generic extension payload, so a new projection type never requires a change to the organisational record model.

projection_id.description: Unique within a run. Not an organisational identifier and never a record id.

projection_type.description: Deliberately an open pattern rather than a closed enum. The six known types validate strictly against their own payload; anything else takes the extension payload and must say why no known type fitted. Adding a type must never require a change to the organisational record model (TDR-0034).

subject_ref.description: What this projection is about — a forum, a control, a mechanism, a decision. An identifier within the reconstruction, not a claim of organisational identity.

source_refs.description: SourceFragment or RecordContribution identifiers behind the projection as a whole. Per-claim provenance lives on each epistemic assessment, which is where GR-01 is enforced.

epistemic_assessments.description: One entry per assessed claim. A forum reconstruction routinely carries several at once — a RECORDED stated purpose, an OBSERVED evidence-assembly job, an INFERRED de-facto authority, an UNKNOWN waiver authority and a CONTRADICTORY accountable owner. One state for the whole projection would destroy exactly the distinction this vocabulary exists to preserve (TDR-0034).

produced_at.description: When this output was generated. Distinct from every assessment's assessment_as_of, and never a substitute for it.

required_authority.description: The authority that would have to be exercised for any recommendation here to be acted on. Naming it is not holding it, and this field never confers it (GR-04, GR-14). There is currently no normative record family this resolves to — the authority language is a candidate package, recorded as an irreducibility finding in TDR-0034.

caveat.description: What a reader must not conclude from this projection beyond what it states.

prohibited_inference.description: Inferences explicitly foreclosed — most usefully, that an unlocatable source makes a mechanism optional, or that an observed decision proves legitimate authority.

carries_standing.description: Structural, not advisory. A projection never carries organisational standing; only an authorised human ratification confers that, evidenced attributably (TDR-0027).

payload.description: Typed by projection_type through the conditional branches below.

epistemicAssessment.description: The epistemic standing of ONE identified claim. Orthogonal to the substrate's uncertainty model and not derivable from it: `derivation` answers how a contribution was produced, the three confidences answer how strong it is, and this answers what standing the projected claim has. RECORDED is not `explicit` — an explicit statement in a meeting pack can be an observation about governance without ever having been admitted organisational state — and an INFERRED claim may carry high epistemic confidence and remain INFERRED.

subject_claim_ref.description: Identifies the claim assessed. Payload fields carrying a claim_ref resolve to one of these; the resolution is checked deterministically by the repository's verification suite.

state.description: RECORDED — supported by organisational state the evidence shows was formally admitted or authoritative FOR THE RELEVANT TIME. OBSERVED — directly evidenced behaviour, artefact or event, WITHOUT asserting authoritative standing. INFERRED — reconstructed from evidence but not directly established. UNKNOWN — insufficient evidence to support a claim. CONTRADICTORY — materially incompatible evidence remains unresolved.

basis_refs.description: What supports the claim. Required for RECORDED, OBSERVED and INFERRED; legitimately empty for UNKNOWN (GR-01).

contradiction_refs.description: The materially incompatible claim or evidence sets. At least two entries where the state is CONTRADICTORY — a contradiction needs both sides on the record.

assessment_as_of.description: The date as of which this state was assessed. Deliberately separate from the envelope's produced_at: a reconstruction of decision-time state is worthless if when a claim was assessed and when the output was generated are conflated (GR-07).

rationale.description: Why this state and not another. Prevents the state becoming an opaque label.

question_asked.description: Required where the state is UNKNOWN: the question that was put to the material.

scope_searched.description: Required where the state is UNKNOWN: what was searched. An UNKNOWN that cannot say what it looked at is an untested absence, not a finding.

finding_type.description: UNCLASSIFIED is a reporting outcome, never a near-fit: a recurring unclassified pattern is evidence for extending the vocabulary by decision, exactly as TDR-0026 established for value contribution classes.

unclassified_note.description: Required where finding_type is UNCLASSIFIED: what was recognised, and why no class fitted.

mandatory_status.description: `unknown` is the honest default. A mechanism whose mandate cannot be located is not thereby discretionary (GR-05).

recommended_disposition.description: RETIRE_CANDIDATE is never executable automatically and is never a decision (GR-10).

job_class.description: ACCOUNTABILITY_ROUTING, not ACCOUNTABILITY: the job a forum performs is routing accountability to a person, never being accountable itself. UNKNOWN where the evidence does not support classification.

holder.description: Who holds it. `unknown` where no source establishes it — never the nearest adjacent holder.

separated_powers.description: Reconstructed separately and never collapsed into one another. An unresolved power stays UNKNOWN through its claim's assessment rather than defaulting to an adjacent holder.

accountability_terminus.description: Terminates in an accountable individual, never a committee abstraction (GR-18).

independence_assessment.description: Multiplicity is not independence: a separate forum, a different name or a distinct reporting line establishes nothing (GR-17).

next_nudge.description: One bounded next change, not a target operating model. Never assumes that more agentic means fewer forums (GR-13).

new_authority_or_delegation_required.description: Required whenever any job is proposed for delegation (GR-14).

population_monitoring_required.description: The population or cohort sensing that must exist before a periodic job may be removed or slowed. Automating transaction-level conformance does not replace a review that saw cohorts (GR-16).

independent_challenge_requirements.description: What must remain true of any challenge function this projection touches. Efficiency never collapses challenge into the execution authority it challenges (GR-15).

accountability_terminus_requirement.description: The named individual in whom accountability terminates after the change, or the statement that it is unresolved (GR-18).

claim_ref.description: One epistemic assessment per material answer — never one state for the whole result.

retrospective_evidence_excluded.description: Material that post-dates the decision and was therefore held out of the reconstruction, named so the exclusion is inspectable (GR-07).

historical_as_of.description: The as-of date the reconstruction is bounded to. Evidence created after this date is retrospective and must be labelled as such.

highest_value_next_evidence.description: The evidence that would most alter the finding — the point of the drill, not a postscript.

reconstruction_metrics.description: Cost, time or effort where the organisation's own data supports it. Absent rather than invented.

phase.description: The default sequence. No first-stage plan places a new commitment mechanism in the critical path.

legal_review_required.description: Privilege, retention, disclosure, regulatory production, complaints evidence and personal data are design inputs, not downstream approvals.

extensionPayload.description: For a projection_type outside the known six. Open by design so the vocabulary can extend without touching the organisational record model — and required to say why no known type fitted, because a recurring extension is evidence for a superseding decision rather than a private convention.

extension_note.description: What this projection carries, and which known type was considered and rejected.
